headline: Anthropic blocks all access to Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5 following US government order
summary: The AI company has suspended global access to its top-tier models after an unprecedented export control directive, citing national security concerns.
details: The US government has issued an unprecedented export control directive ordering Anthropic to immediately suspend all access to its top-tier Claude Fable 5 and Claude Mythos 5 models for foreign nationals, citing unspecified national security authorities.

In response, Anthropic has blocked all public access to both models globally. This is a significant reversal, as Fable/Mythos 5 were only publicly released three days prior. Current sessions will end in errors, and new queries will be routed to older, less capable models.

Anthropic stated, "We believe this is a misunderstanding and are working to restore access as soon as possible," and apologized to its customers. The sudden regulatory intervention highlights how centralized, cloud-based frontier models are subject to government oversight.

The government's action follows a viral jailbreak of Fable 5 published on X, where the user claimed to have bypassed safety guardrails to extract instructions for cyber exploits, explosives, and chemical synthesis. Anthropic noted that the government's evidence of a specific jailbreak has been poorly documented.

Anthropic argues that the capabilities uncovered are "widely available" in other public models, including OpenAI's GPT-5.5. They warn that blocking a commercial model over a non-universal jailbreak could halt all new model deployments for frontier model providers.

This sudden blackout of Anthropic's latest AI models will cause consternation for organizations relying on the Claude API. It underscores the operational risk of running critical workflows on any single AI model or provider, as it creates a single point of failure.

Anthropic confirmed that access to all other Claude models will not be affected. However, the US government's order serves as a stark warning, as future actions could potentially target all of a lab's AI models and services.

This situation echoes a previous incident in March 2026, when the Pentagon labeled Anthropic a "supply chain risk" after the company refused to allow the military to use Claude for mass domestic surveillance and lethal autonomous weapons without safety restrictions.
